en.title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays of Equal Length
en.description:
Merge two non-decreasing arrays into one non-decreasing array, keeping all duplicate values.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and solution; bounds missing from the source and corrections to the examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains the common length n, followed by two lines each with n integers. Full original bounds: 1<n≤100000, 0≤element≤10^9, and each array is non-decreasing.
en.output: Output the 2n merged integers, separated by spaces. The original return signature int[n] does not match the statement, so all 2n items are kept here as the statement requires.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 1 2 2 3 5 5; 0 0 0 1; 1 3 4 5. They were verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Use two pointers to compare the smallest values not yet output and take the smaller one; once one side is exhausted, output the rest of the other side.
